newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed in Europe on Monday from New York's closing levels as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of a batch of economic data as well as the Fed's regular monetary meeting.
"It's been very quiet. Institutions don't want to do much with the Fed meeting tomorrow," one market maker said. "If we get some bad payroll numbers on Friday the market could see the bears return."
The main focus of attention will be the latest survey from the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM), due at 1500 GMT, dealers said.
The FOMC meeting, scheduled to take place on Tuesday and Wednesday, will also be watched, although many economists do not expect the Fed to move on interest rates this week.
The key U.S. unemployment figures, including the non-farm payroll total, are due on Friday.
Gillette was up $1.5 at $83 after the company reported after the Dow's close on Friday, Q4 earnings of $0.21 a share compared with $0.64 in the same period a year ago.
The Q4 EPS included a $0.51 per share charge for merger costs. "The figures were pretty good when you strip out the exceptional charge," one dealer said.
Apple Computer was unchanged at $16-5/8 after press reports that the company is considering selling key business units to step up its cost-cutting efforts.
On Sunday a source close to Apple told Reuters that the company plans to cut its operations to three groups and announce on Monday a round of massive job cuts.
The S&P 500 futures contract on the Globex after-hours trading system, was up 0.45 at 787.95 by 1100 GMT. The March T-bond was down 3/32 at 111-11/32.
